items.name: Food effect on AUC (fold-change)
items.definition: Fold-change in AUC due to food effect on oral absorption, as reported in clinical pharmacology studies or labels. A value of 1 indicates no food effect; values greater than 1 indicate increased exposure with food.

items.name: Lipinski rule of 5 violation count
items.definition: Number of Lipinski rule-of-five violations (molecular weight > 500, logP > 5, hydrogen-bond donors > 5, hydrogen-bond acceptors > 10) computed from the compound structure; lower counts indicate better oral drug-likeness and absorption potential. Values pooled from the contributing sources are reduced by median.

items.name: Lipophilicity (logP) within optimal kinase-inhibitor range
items.definition: Computed XLogP (log units) from PubChem. The source states moderate lipophilicity (logP ≈ 2–4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors; candidates are ranked by distance outside this band, with values inside the band scoring best.

evaluation.reason: preference has no executable predicate: 'range_membership' needs a declared comparison cutoff; no cutoff or pass value is inferred

items.name: Molecular weight (Da)
items.definition: Molecular weight of the compound in Daltons (g/mol), computed from structure by the curated descriptor route rather than a trained prediction; lower values are preferred because size above roughly 500 Da approaches the upper limit compatible with efficient passive intestinal diffusion and increases efflux-transporter recognition.

items.name: Oral administration route (recorded)
items.definition: Whether the compound is documented as orally administered in humans (e.g., approved oral drug, clinical trial oral dosing). This is a preference, not a requirement: absence of documentation gives unknown, never fail, because the oral route may simply be undocumented.

items.name: Oral bioavailability (human, measured F%)
items.definition: Reported absolute or relative oral bioavailability (F%) in humans, as a measured pharmacokinetic parameter. Higher values indicate greater fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation intact. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.

items.name: Predicted aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
items.definition: Model-predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model; recorded as a descriptive consideration because the cited claims report solubility as a generic drug-like property and give low-solubility examples, without validating this endpoint or establishing a direction for this library.

items.name: Predicted blood-brain barrier penetration probability (BBB_Martins)
items.definition: Model-predicted probability of blood-brain barrier penetration; lower probability is generally preferred for peripheral targets to minimise CNS side effects.

items.name: Predicted BRENK alert count
items.definition: Number of BRENK alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of problematic substructures.

items.name: Predicted Caco-2 permeability (ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang, log 10^-6 cm/s)

items.name: Predicted clinical toxicity probability (exploratory)
items.definition: ADMET-AI ClinTox model output: predicted probability in [0,1] of clinical toxicity. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents general toxicity and dose-limiting adverse events for this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

items.name: Predicted CYP1A2 inhibition probability
items.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP1A2, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.

items.name: FGFR1 potency threshold
items.definition: Binary indicator of whether the compound has a reported FGFR1 inhibitory concentration below 20 nM, based on literature evidence.
items.reason: Two material findings. (1) claim_01M4X8B2WTZH1PSG3BHVZXST80 states that representative FGFR inhibitors block FGFR activity at concentrations less than 20 nM, but it does not establish 20 nM as a screening cutoff for this library, and the cited compounds are not the candidates being screened; the source number is a reported observation about a named set, not a decision threshold for this population. (2) The attribute is defined as a binary indicator with direction lower_better while the rule is a threshold preference, an incoherent combination. The cutoff could only be salvaged by declaring an interpretation (reports_measurement, at_most_the_reported_value) with a population rationale, but the population rationale would be circular because the 20 nM figure describes a different, named compound set rather than the screened library. Withdraw rather than retain an unsupported cutoff.

after.reason: The validator notes that literature evidence yields numbers with units, so a literature-bound attribute must be quantitative with a unit. The cited claims report food effects on AUC and Cmax for specific agents, which are quantitative measurements. location.quoted_span: The primary impediment obstructing the therapeutic advancement of AE is its inadequate “druglikeness,” particularly regarding its pharmacokinetic properties. A characteristic attribute of AE is its markedly low water solubility, which significantly limits the options for its formulations and its dissolving within the gastrointestinal tract (Ai et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2023). Following oral ingestion, it experiences significant first-pass metabolism in the liver and intestinal wall, primarily by glucuronidation and sulfation, and is swiftly digested (Ren et al., 2024; El-Say et al., 2023; Kumar et al., 2024). The synergistic impact of inadequate absorption and accelerated metabolism results in exceedingly low oral bioavailability, often ranging from 1% to 5%, complicating the attainment and maintenance of an effective plasma therapeutic dosage via standard oral administration

conclusion.text: The criterion treats a lower predicted BRENK alert count as preferable, using a deterministic RDKit-derived count of problematic substructures as a class-level heuristic for toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics. It is a preference ordering, not a measured safety outcome, and the source claim does not report BRENK alerts or any toxicity data.

conditions.text: Applicability assumes a computable structure and the ADMET-AI BRENK_alert endpoint, with values sourced as database entries and determination treated as derived. The ordering is meaningful only if BRENK alerts track toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics in the relevant chemical space.

limitations.text: The source claim concerns combination therapy and drug-drug interaction risk, not BRENK alerts, so it does not validate the alert-to-safety link. No reference-set correlation, threshold, population, assay or units are provided, and the falsification test remains untested. Whether alert counts predict toxicity or pharmacokinetics for these compounds is unknown.

task_implication.text: For this oral multi-target agent task, the criterion offers a structural-liability signal that can be applied uniformly to every compound with a structure, complementing target-engagement evidence when comparing candidates. It does not itself establish CSF1R, VEGFR1-3 or FGFR1 activity, oral exposure, or clinical suitability.

location.quoted_span: Small-molecule TKIs are administered orally, which likely contributes to variability in TKI exposure [48]. Absorption is the process underlying entry into systemic circulation after oral administration and a significant determinant of oral bioavailability. To be absorbed, a solid dosage form must be dissolved and solubilized before being transported or diffusing across the gut lumen. While disintegration and solubilization mainly occur in the mouth and stomach, the transporter-mediated absorption of most drugs is believed to primarily occur in the small intestine due to its exceptionally high surface area. However, the stomach has been validated to contribute to the transporter-mediated absorption of dasatinib, emphasizing the notion that drug absorption is complex [49]. pH-dependent solubility, gastric emptying time, inhibition of uptake and efflux transporters, and inhibition or induction of enterocyte cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzyme CYP3A4 can also contribute to clinically relevant absorption DDIs [13,16]

source.excerpt: Futibatinib is metabolized in the liver largely through the CYP 3A4 pathway and liver injury might be caused by production of a toxic or immunogenic intermediate. Because it is a substrate for CYP 3A4, futibatinib is susceptible to drug-drug interactions with agents that inhibit or induce this specific hepatic microsomal activity

location.quoted_span: Small-molecule TKIs are administered orally, which likely contributes to variability in TKI exposure [48]. Absorption is the process underlying entry into systemic circulation after oral administration and a significant determinant of oral bioavailability. To be absorbed, a solid dosage form must be dissolved and solubilized before being transported or diffusing across the gut lumen. While disintegration and solubilization mainly occur in the mouth and stomach, the transporter-mediated absorption of most drugs is believed to primarily occur in the small intestine due to its exceptionally high surface area. However, the stomach has been validated to contribute to the transporter-mediated absorption of dasatinib, emphasizing the notion that drug absorption is complex [49]. pH-dependent solubility, gastric emptying time, inhibition of uptake and efflux transporters, and inhibition or induction of enterocyte cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzyme CYP3A4 can also contribute to clinically relevant absorption DDIs [13,16]

location.quoted_span: The primary impediment obstructing the therapeutic advancement of AE is its inadequate “druglikeness,” particularly regarding its pharmacokinetic properties. A characteristic attribute of AE is its markedly low water solubility, which significantly limits the options for its formulations and its dissolving within the gastrointestinal tract (Ai et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2023). Following oral ingestion, it experiences significant first-pass metabolism in the liver and intestinal wall, primarily by glucuronidation and sulfation, and is swiftly digested (Ren et al., 2024; El-Say et al., 2023; Kumar et al., 2024). The synergistic impact of inadequate absorption and accelerated metabolism results in exceedingly low oral bioavailability, often ranging from 1% to 5%, complicating the attainment and maintenance of an effective plasma therapeutic dosage via standard oral administration

Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

details.name: VEGFR3 curated potency
details.definition: Median curated pChEMBL potency for the compound against VEGFR3 (CHEMBL1955), pooled across ChEMBL and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology curated measurements.
details.reason: The eight members measure the same quantity, curated pChEMBL potency against VEGFR3 (CHEMBL1955), in the same unit and direction (higher_better) with the same measurement kind, value sources and determination bases. nodes.name: VEGFR3 curated potency

nodes.name: VEGFR3 curated potency (pChEMBL, pooled ChEMBL + IUPHAR)
nodes.definition: Median curated pChEMBL value (pChEMBL = -log10 molar IC50/Ki/Kd/EC50) for the compound against VEGFR3 (CHEMBL1955), pooled from ChEMBL curated activity records and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology affinity records; higher pChEMBL indicates stronger VEGFR3 engagement.

attribute.definition: Median curated pChEMBL potency for the compound against VEGFR3 (CHEMBL1955), pooled across ChEMBL and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology curated measurements.
attribute.name: VEGFR3 curated potency
attribute.rationale: VEGFR3 is a required target. Curated potency measurements provide the quantitative engagement evidence. No cited claim states a numeric pChEMBL threshold for VEGFR3, so the rule ranks by ordering rather than applying a cutoff.

raw.expected_change: Ranks candidates by measured VEGFR3 potency.
raw.falsification_test: If a candidate with no VEGFR3 pChEMBL record is later shown to be a potent VEGFR3 inhibitor, the preference ordering would be misleading; the candidate remains in the pool with unknown status.

explanation.decision_question: Which candidates have a more favourable VEGFR3 curated potency?
explanation.how_evaluated: Use the accepted source values without an added transformation. Combine usable values using median. Order available values with larger values preferred; no cutoff is applied.
explanation.why_included: VEGFR3 is a required target. Curated potency measurements provide the quantitative engagement evidence. No cited claim states a numeric pChEMBL threshold for VEGFR3, so the rule ranks by ordering rather than applying a cutoff.

details.reason: All eight members measure one quantity: median curated pChEMBL potency against FGFR1 (CHEMBL3650) at higher-is-better in pChEMBL. They agree on unit, direction, measurement kind, value sources (curated_measurement) and determination basis (measured), and differ only in which curated databases answer the same question (ChEMBL pChEMBL values, IUPHAR/BPS affinity) and in rule bookkeeping fields, so the members are one measurement restated and merge into a single pooled criterion that reads both routes.

details.name: FGFR1 potency threshold
details.definition: Binary indicator of whether the compound has a reported FGFR1 inhibitory concentration below 20 nM, based on literature evidence.
details.reason: Two material findings. (1) claim_01M4X8B2WTZH1PSG3BHVZXST80 states that representative FGFR inhibitors block FGFR activity at concentrations less than 20 nM, but it does not establish 20 nM as a screening cutoff for this library, and the cited compounds are not the candidates being screened; the source number is a reported observation about a named set, not a decision threshold for this population. (2) The attribute is defined as a binary indicator with direction lower_better while the rule is a threshold preference, an incoherent combination. The cutoff could only be salvaged by declaring an interpretation (reports_measurement, at_most_the_reported_value) with a population rationale, but the population rationale would be circular because the 20 nM figure describes a different, named compound set rather than the screened library. Withdraw rather than retain an unsupported cutoff.

details.name: FGFR1 curated potency (pChEMBL)
details.definition: Median curated pChEMBL potency value for the compound against FGFR1 (CHEMBL3650), pooled from ChEMBL and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology curated measurements; higher pChEMBL indicates stronger FGFR1 engagement.

details.reason: All seven members measure one and the same quantity: curated pChEMBL potency of the compound against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844). They agree on unit (pChEMBL), direction (higher_better), measurement kind (quantitative), value sources (curated_measurement) and determination bases (measured), and they differ only in wording and in which curation answers the question (ChEMBL activity records versus IUPHAR/BPS affinity records). That is the same measurement curated by two sources, so it is one criterion; the merged attribute keeps the clearest definition, carries both curated routes, and inherits the median aggregation all members use. Differences in on_missing/on_conflict handling are rule-level and do not split the quantity.

details.definition: Median curated pChEMBL potency (=-log10 molar IC50/Ki/Kd/EC50) for the compound against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844), pooled across ChEMBL and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology curation.
details.reason: All seven members measure one and the same quantity: curated pChEMBL potency of the compound against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844). They agree on unit (pChEMBL), direction (higher_better), measurement kind (quantitative), value sources (curated_measurement) and determination bases (measured), and they differ only in wording and in which curation answers the question (ChEMBL activity records versus IUPHAR/BPS affinity records). That is the same measurement curated by two sources, so it is one criterion; the merged attribute keeps the clearest definition, carries both curated routes, and inherits the median aggregation all members use. Differences in on_missing/on_conflict handling are rule-level and do not split the quantity.

location.quoted_span: Macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) is essential for the entire process from the production of osteoclast precursors to the formation and survival of mature osteoclasts. Upon M-CSF binding to its receptor c-Fms (CSF1R), the receptor is phosphorylated at a specific tyrosine residue in its cytoplasmic tail. These phosphorylated tyrosine residues on the receptor recruit signaling molecules such as growth factor receptor-bound protein 2 (Grb2) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K). This process triggers the activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) and protein kinase B (Akt) pathways, which promote the survival and proliferation of osteoclast precursors

location.quoted_span: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

source.title: Colorectal cancer pathogenesis, oncogenic signaling networks and targeted therapeutic advances
source.excerpt: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

location.quoted_span: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]
section_path: Molecular pathogenesis: foundation for targeted therapy
Signaling pathways in colorectal cancer tumorigenesis

location.quoted_span: Macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) is essential for the entire process from the production of osteoclast precursors to the formation and survival of mature osteoclasts. Upon M-CSF binding to its receptor c-Fms (CSF1R), the receptor is phosphorylated at a specific tyrosine residue in its cytoplasmic tail. These phosphorylated tyrosine residues on the receptor recruit signaling molecules such as growth factor receptor-bound protein 2 (Grb2) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K). This process triggers the activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) and protein kinase B (Akt) pathways, which promote the survival and proliferation of osteoclast precursors

location.quoted_span: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

location.quoted_span: Macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) is essential for the entire process from the production of osteoclast precursors to the formation and survival of mature osteoclasts. Upon M-CSF binding to its receptor c-Fms (CSF1R), the receptor is phosphorylated at a specific tyrosine residue in its cytoplasmic tail. These phosphorylated tyrosine residues on the receptor recruit signaling molecules such as growth factor receptor-bound protein 2 (Grb2) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K). This process triggers the activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) and protein kinase B (Akt) pathways, which promote the survival and proliferation of osteoclast precursors

location.quoted_span: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

sources.quote: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

This process triggers the activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) and protein kinase B (Akt) pathways, which promote the survival and proliferation of osteoclast precursors

location.quoted_span: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

location.quoted_span: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]
section_path: Molecular pathogenesis: foundation for targeted therapy
Signaling pathways in colorectal cancer tumorigenesis

details.name: Selectivity against FGFR4 (potency gap)

details.reason: The value_transform basis is invalid under the schema, and the cited claim (FGFR1-FGFR4 homology) supports only that selectivity is challenging, not that an FGFR1-over-FGFR4 potency gap is a decision-relevant preference for this task. FGFR4 is not a required target, so the gap does not bear on concurrent engagement of the five required targets. Withdrawn rather than revised because the evidence does not support the property.

details.definition: Median curated pChEMBL potency for the compound against FGFR1 (CHEMBL3650) meets or exceeds 6 (corresponding to IC50/Ki/Kd <= 1 µM), a common threshold for meaningful target engagement.
details.reason: The critic is correct on both counts. (1) The cited claims (erdafitinib, dovitinib, rogaratinib, futibatinib, pemigatinib, infigratinib) assert FGFR1-4 inhibition as a qualitative target-coverage statement; none reports a pChEMBL value, an IC50, or any numeric potency for FGFR1, so no cited claim states a number that could serve as the pChEMBL >= 6 cutoff. The cutoff is therefore unsupported and the attribute would rank on an invented threshold. (2) The attribute scores only FGFR1, which is one of five required targets; a single-target potency criterion does not by itself satisfy the concurrent five-target objective and duplicates the registry's existing 'FGFR1 curated potency' criterion. Withdrawing rather than revising because the registry already carries per-target curated potency criteria for all five targets, so a re-worded single-target FGFR1 potency attribute would be a duplicate, and no cited claim supplies a defensible numeric cutoff to convert it into a threshold rule.

details.reason: All seven members measure one and the same quantity: curated pChEMBL potency of the compound against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844). They agree on unit (pChEMBL), direction (higher_better), measurement kind (quantitative), value sources (curated_measurement) and determination bases (measured), and they differ only in wording and in which curation answers the question (ChEMBL activity records versus IUPHAR/BPS affinity records). That is the same measurement curated by two sources, so it is one criterion; the merged attribute keeps the clearest definition, carries both curated routes, and inherits the median aggregation all members use. Differences in on_missing/on_conflict handling are rule-level and do not split the quantity.

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%) threshold
attribute.rationale: A threshold on human F% operationalizes the oral bioavailability requirement. The registry already contains 'Human oral bioavailability (measured F%) threshold'; this proposal is distinct in specifying a 30% cutoff and providing bound_support records for the cutoff. The cutoff is derived from the reported range of F% values in the claims (39%, 57%, 36%, 43%, 50%, 81%, 27.5%, 38%, 16.4%, 4.9%, 2.2%, 6.8%, 3.5%) and the heuristic that F% >= 30% is generally considered adequate for oral development.

raw.expected_change: Ranks candidates with measured human F% >= 30% above those with lower values; candidates with F% < 30% are deprioritized but not excluded.
raw.falsification_test: If a compound with measured human F% < 30% achieves clinical efficacy at an oral dose comparable to high-F% candidates, the 30% threshold would be falsified as a decision-relevant cutoff.

location.quoted_span: Small-molecule TKIs are administered orally, which likely contributes to variability in TKI exposure [48]. Absorption is the process underlying entry into systemic circulation after oral administration and a significant determinant of oral bioavailability. To be absorbed, a solid dosage form must be dissolved and solubilized before being transported or diffusing across the gut lumen. While disintegration and solubilization mainly occur in the mouth and stomach, the transporter-mediated absorption of most drugs is believed to primarily occur in the small intestine due to its exceptionally high surface area. However, the stomach has been validated to contribute to the transporter-mediated absorption of dasatinib, emphasizing the notion that drug absorption is complex [49]. pH-dependent solubility, gastric emptying time, inhibition of uptake and efflux transporters, and inhibition or induction of enterocyte cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzyme CYP3A4 can also contribute to clinically relevant absorption DDIs [13,16]

location.quoted_span: Small-molecule TKIs are administered orally, which likely contributes to variability in TKI exposure [48]. Absorption is the process underlying entry into systemic circulation after oral administration and a significant determinant of oral bioavailability. To be absorbed, a solid dosage form must be dissolved and solubilized before being transported or diffusing across the gut lumen. While disintegration and solubilization mainly occur in the mouth and stomach, the transporter-mediated absorption of most drugs is believed to primarily occur in the small intestine due to its exceptionally high surface area. However, the stomach has been validated to contribute to the transporter-mediated absorption of dasatinib, emphasizing the notion that drug absorption is complex [49]. pH-dependent solubility, gastric emptying time, inhibition of uptake and efflux transporters, and inhibition or induction of enterocyte cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzyme CYP3A4 can also contribute to clinically relevant absorption DDIs [13,16]

location.quoted_span: Small-molecule TKIs are administered orally, which likely contributes to variability in TKI exposure [48]. Absorption is the process underlying entry into systemic circulation after oral administration and a significant determinant of oral bioavailability. To be absorbed, a solid dosage form must be dissolved and solubilized before being transported or diffusing across the gut lumen. While disintegration and solubilization mainly occur in the mouth and stomach, the transporter-mediated absorption of most drugs is believed to primarily occur in the small intestine due to its exceptionally high surface area. However, the stomach has been validated to contribute to the transporter-mediated absorption of dasatinib, emphasizing the notion that drug absorption is complex [49]. pH-dependent solubility, gastric emptying time, inhibition of uptake and efflux transporters, and inhibition or induction of enterocyte cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzyme CYP3A4 can also contribute to clinically relevant absorption DDIs [13,16]

location.quoted_span: Although oral administration is convenient, ICA exhibits low oral bioavailability (~12%) due to poor intestinal absorption and extensive first-pass metabolism, limiting its therapeutic efficacy in bone-related disorders, as shown in Table 2 [51]. Bioavailability determines systemic exposure and directly affects therapeutic efficacy, making the improvement of ICA absorption essential for its further development in bone-related disorders [52]. Among the main determinants of oral absorption, aqueous solubility and membrane permeability are particularly important, since a drug must first dissolve in gastrointestinal fluid and then cross the epithelial barrier to reach the circulation; insufficient solubility therefore commonly leads to limited absorption and reduced pharmacological effect [53]

location.quoted_span: From a pharmacokinetic perspective, imatinib exhibits rapid oral bioavailability that is not significantly affected by food intake. It has a half‐life of approximately 18 h and is highly protein‐bound (95%), primarily to albumin and α1‐acid glycoprotein. Metabolism is predominantly hepatic, mediated by the CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 enzymes. Notably, imatinib also acts as a competitive inhibitor of these enzymes, creating a significant potential for drug–drug interactions with other PAH therapies metabolized via the same pathway [81]. Elimination is primarily biliary, with a feces‐to‐urine excretion ratio of approximately 5:1

details.name: Predicted heavy atom count
details.definition: Number of heavy atoms, computed by RDKit from the structure.
details.reason: The validator is correct that the ADMET-AI catalog entry defines no HeavyAtomCount endpoint (the endpoint list contains molecular_weight, logP, hydrogen_bond_acceptors/donors, Lipinski, QED, stereo_centers, tpsa, PAINS/BRENK/NIH alerts and the ADMET endpoints, but no HeavyAtomCount), so the evidence_request cannot be bound and the attribute would carry no evidence. Independently, the only cited claim (claim_01M4YT2WE3T610NCGNXPPW03AZ) is a statement about drug-drug interaction risk in combination therapy and says nothing about heavy atom count or drug-likeness, so the supporting_claim_ids entry is unsupported. The property is also a generic size descriptor that does not measure concurrent CSF1R/VEGFR1/VEGFR2/VEGFR3/FGFR1 engagement or oral suitability, and no cited passage states any number that could serve as a cutoff. Withdrawing rather than re-binding to property_estimate/computed_property, since that would be a new proposal and the claim support would still be absent.

details.name: Predicted heavy atom count
details.definition: Number of heavy atoms computed by RDKit from the structure via the ADMET-AI panel. Lower counts are generally favourable for drug-likeness.
details.reason: The validator is correct that the ADMET-AI route has no declared output for endpoint 'HeavyAtomCount' (the panel offers molecular_weight, logP, hydrogen_bond_acceptors/donors, Lipinski, QED, stereo_centers, tpsa, PAINS/BRENK/NIH alerts, not HeavyAtomCount), so the attribute can never be populated. The only cited claim (claim_01M4YTGHTTBN4NVPS85SAVFS32) is a generic enumeration of ligand-design descriptor classes and states no number, so no cutoff is available either. Heavy atom count is also a general size descriptor that does not serve the objective of concurrent engagement of CSF1R/VEGFR1/VEGFR2/VEGFR3/FGFR1, and the same size information is already carried by the molecular-weight descriptor route. Withdraw rather than substitute a different endpoint, since adding new proposals is out of scope.

A general PK descriptor with no informative model and no transferable threshold does not serve the objective of identifying a compound concurrently engaging the five specified targets.

Elimination is primarily biliary, with a feces‐to‐urine excretion ratio of approximately 5:1

location.quoted_span: The primary impediment obstructing the therapeutic advancement of AE is its inadequate “druglikeness,” particularly regarding its pharmacokinetic properties. A characteristic attribute of AE is its markedly low water solubility, which significantly limits the options for its formulations and its dissolving within the gastrointestinal tract (Ai et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2023). Following oral ingestion, it experiences significant first-pass metabolism in the liver and intestinal wall, primarily by glucuronidation and sulfation, and is swiftly digested (Ren et al., 2024; El-Say et al., 2023; Kumar et al., 2024). The synergistic impact of inadequate absorption and accelerated metabolism results in exceedingly low oral bioavailability, often ranging from 1% to 5%, complicating the attainment and maintenance of an effective plasma therapeutic dosage via standard oral administration

location.quoted_span: The primary impediment obstructing the therapeutic advancement of AE is its inadequate “druglikeness,” particularly regarding its pharmacokinetic properties. A characteristic attribute of AE is its markedly low water solubility, which significantly limits the options for its formulations and its dissolving within the gastrointestinal tract (Ai et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2023). Following oral ingestion, it experiences significant first-pass metabolism in the liver and intestinal wall, primarily by glucuronidation and sulfation, and is swiftly digested (Ren et al., 2024; El-Say et al., 2023; Kumar et al., 2024). The synergistic impact of inadequate absorption and accelerated metabolism results in exceedingly low oral bioavailability, often ranging from 1% to 5%, complicating the attainment and maintenance of an effective plasma therapeutic dosage via standard oral administration

location.quoted_span: From a pharmacokinetic perspective, imatinib exhibits rapid oral bioavailability that is not significantly affected by food intake. It has a half‐life of approximately 18 h and is highly protein‐bound (95%), primarily to albumin and α1‐acid glycoprotein. Metabolism is predominantly hepatic, mediated by the CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 enzymes. Notably, imatinib also acts as a competitive inhibitor of these enzymes, creating a significant potential for drug–drug interactions with other PAH therapies metabolized via the same pathway [81]. Elimination is primarily biliary, with a feces‐to‐urine excretion ratio of approximately 5:1

details.reason: All seven members measure one quantity: an ADMET model-predicted Skin_Reaction probability, in the same unit (probability), same direction (lower_better), same source (model_prediction) and same determination basis (predicted), for the same purpose (dermatologic-tolerability preference for a chronically dosed oral agent). They differ only in how repeated predicted values are pooled (median vs max) and in rule flavour (one exploratory consideration, the rest preferences, two of them carrying an unspecified-strength 0.5 model-decision-boundary threshold). None of those is one of the quantity fields the members already agree on, so the quantity merges; the merged criterion takes the worst-case (maximum) pooling that fits the lower_better direction, and the majority rule, a preference with no numeric cutoff because most members found the evidence insufficient to assert one.

The cutoff_basis 'model_decision_boundary' is also invalid here: the catalog restricts that basis to the natural 0.5 boundary of a binary classifier, whereas Lipophilicity_AstraZeneca is a regression endpoint with no stated decision boundary, and no cited claim supplies a number to threshold on. Withdrawing rather than inventing a bound.

details.name: Predicted blood-brain barrier penetration probability (BBB_Martins)

details.reason: Two material findings stand: (1) the cited claim lists sunitinib adverse events and does not mention blood-brain barrier penetration or CNS toxicity, so it supports neither the attribute nor the 0.5 cutoff; (2) the objective is target engagement by an orally administered agent, and a preference for lower BBB penetration is a safety consideration not tied to that objective and could deprioritize otherwise suitable agents. Withdrawing.

attribute.name: Predicted microsomal intrinsic clearance
attribute.rationale: High microsomal clearance can necessitate higher doses, potentially increasing toxicity; the model provides a quantitative estimate for all compounds with structures. The cited claim supplies a measured clearance value in the same class, used here as a cross-system reference bound for a preference.

raw.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted microsomal clearance above those with higher clearance, favouring candidates with better exposure and potentially lower toxicity.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim reports a measured hepatocyte intrinsic clearance for a compound in this class; the same numeric value is used as a preference bound on the microsomal clearance scale because both express intrinsic clearance in the same class and the bound is a ranking preference, not an exclusion.

interpretation.measurement: Mouse hepatocyte intrinsic clearance of 70.6 ± 5.4 uL/min/10^6 cells for a compound in this class, described as high.
interpretation.population_rationale: Candidates are orally administered kinase inhibitors in the same series; a microsomal clearance at or below the reported hepatocyte value is a reasonable preference bound for acceptable exposure, while higher values are disfavoured rather than excluded.

location.quoted_span: Therefore, the safety margin for QT-interval prolongation (only the most stringent margin was taken into account for the calculation) of the compound’s total concentration in human plasma was 46.5 μM (or 20.8 μg/mL) ( Supplementary Table 6B ). In PK studies in mice, the PK profile of CPL304110 administered at an effective dose (40 mg/kg, p.o.) showed a Cmax of 4.01 μg/mL (see further sections), which was below the calculated safety margin. Thus, we concluded that the compound CPL304110 did not pose a risk in terms of cardiac safety

summary.text: The safety margin for QT-interval prolongation based on total plasma concentration was 46.5 micromolar (20.8 µg/mL), and in mice the effective oral dose of 40 mg/kg gave a Cmax of 4.01 µg/mL, below that margin, so the compound was concluded not to pose a cardiac safety risk.

location.quoted_span: The primary impediment obstructing the therapeutic advancement of AE is its inadequate “druglikeness,” particularly regarding its pharmacokinetic properties. A characteristic attribute of AE is its markedly low water solubility, which significantly limits the options for its formulations and its dissolving within the gastrointestinal tract (Ai et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2023). Following oral ingestion, it experiences significant first-pass metabolism in the liver and intestinal wall, primarily by glucuronidation and sulfation, and is swiftly digested (Ren et al., 2024; El-Say et al., 2023; Kumar et al., 2024). The synergistic impact of inadequate absorption and accelerated metabolism results in exceedingly low oral bioavailability, often ranging from 1% to 5%, complicating the attainment and maintenance of an effective plasma therapeutic dosage via standard oral administration

location.quoted_span: Small-molecule TKIs are administered orally, which likely contributes to variability in TKI exposure [48]. Absorption is the process underlying entry into systemic circulation after oral administration and a significant determinant of oral bioavailability. To be absorbed, a solid dosage form must be dissolved and solubilized before being transported or diffusing across the gut lumen. While disintegration and solubilization mainly occur in the mouth and stomach, the transporter-mediated absorption of most drugs is believed to primarily occur in the small intestine due to its exceptionally high surface area. However, the stomach has been validated to contribute to the transporter-mediated absorption of dasatinib, emphasizing the notion that drug absorption is complex [49]. pH-dependent solubility, gastric emptying time, inhibition of uptake and efflux transporters, and inhibition or induction of enterocyte cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzyme CYP3A4 can also contribute to clinically relevant absorption DDIs [13,16]

location.quoted_span: The primary impediment obstructing the therapeutic advancement of AE is its inadequate “druglikeness,” particularly regarding its pharmacokinetic properties. A characteristic attribute of AE is its markedly low water solubility, which significantly limits the options for its formulations and its dissolving within the gastrointestinal tract (Ai et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2023). Following oral ingestion, it experiences significant first-pass metabolism in the liver and intestinal wall, primarily by glucuronidation and sulfation, and is swiftly digested (Ren et al., 2024; El-Say et al., 2023; Kumar et al., 2024). The synergistic impact of inadequate absorption and accelerated metabolism results in exceedingly low oral bioavailability, often ranging from 1% to 5%, complicating the attainment and maintenance of an effective plasma therapeutic dosage via standard oral administration

location.quoted_span: Small-molecule TKIs are administered orally, which likely contributes to variability in TKI exposure [48]. Absorption is the process underlying entry into systemic circulation after oral administration and a significant determinant of oral bioavailability. To be absorbed, a solid dosage form must be dissolved and solubilized before being transported or diffusing across the gut lumen. While disintegration and solubilization mainly occur in the mouth and stomach, the transporter-mediated absorption of most drugs is believed to primarily occur in the small intestine due to its exceptionally high surface area. However, the stomach has been validated to contribute to the transporter-mediated absorption of dasatinib, emphasizing the notion that drug absorption is complex [49]. pH-dependent solubility, gastric emptying time, inhibition of uptake and efflux transporters, and inhibition or induction of enterocyte cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzyme CYP3A4 can also contribute to clinically relevant absorption DDIs [13,16]

location.quoted_span: Infigratinib (BGJ398), a selective oral inhibitor of FGFR1-FGFR3 received accelerated U.S. FDA approval based on data from a single-arm Phase II trial for the treatment of previously treated patients with locally advanced or metastatic CCA with FGFR2 fusion or reconfiguration. A total of 122 patients, 108 with FGFR2 fusion and rearrangement and at least one systemic treatment, were enrolled in the clinical trial and were scheduled to receive 125 mg infigratinib for 1–21 days and 22–28 days of discontinuation. Infigratinib in these patients, second-line treatment ORR was 23.1%, DCR was 84.3%, mPFS was 7.3 months, and mOS was 11.8 months. Hyperphosphatemia, stomatitis, fatigue, and hair loss were the most common adverse events. Grade III or worse AEs occurred in 64% of patients, and six grade IV adverse events were laboratory abnormalities [36]

location.quoted_span: The metabolic reliance on the CYP3A4 pathway renders imatinib highly susceptible to interactions, a factor of paramount importance in the PAH population. CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, erythromycin) can elevate imatinib plasma levels, increasing toxicity risks, while CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's wort) may lead to subtherapeutic exposure. Furthermore, as an inhibitor of CYP3A4 itself, imatinib can increase the systemic concentration of co‐administered agents like simvastatin or cyclosporine

details.name: Predicted skin reaction probability
details.definition: Model-predicted probability that a compound elicits a skin reaction (rash, hand-foot skin reaction), a frequently reported adverse event class for chronically dosed oral kinase inhibitors; used as a computable tolerability surrogate for the whole library.
details.reason: All seven members measure one quantity: an ADMET model-predicted Skin_Reaction probability, in the same unit (probability), same direction (lower_better), same source (model_prediction) and same determination basis (predicted), for the same purpose (dermatologic-tolerability preference for a chronically dosed oral agent). They differ only in how repeated predicted values are pooled (median vs max) and in rule flavour (one exploratory consideration, the rest preferences, two of them carrying an unspecified-strength 0.5 model-decision-boundary threshold). None of those is one of the quantity fields the members already agree on, so the quantity merges; the merged criterion takes the worst-case (maximum) pooling that fits the lower_better direction, and the majority rule, a preference with no numeric cutoff because most members found the evidence insufficient to assert one.

location.quoted_span: Macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) is essential for the entire process from the production of osteoclast precursors to the formation and survival of mature osteoclasts. Upon M-CSF binding to its receptor c-Fms (CSF1R), the receptor is phosphorylated at a specific tyrosine residue in its cytoplasmic tail. These phosphorylated tyrosine residues on the receptor recruit signaling molecules such as growth factor receptor-bound protein 2 (Grb2) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K). This process triggers the activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) and protein kinase B (Akt) pathways, which promote the survival and proliferation of osteoclast precursors

location.quoted_span: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

sources.quote: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

source.excerpt: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]

location.quoted_span: The VEGF pathway is crucial for CRC angiogenesis and metastasis. The VEGF ligands (VEGFA-D and PlGF) signal through three tyrosine kinase receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3) as well as the coreceptors neuropilin-1 and neuropilin-2 [97]. VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis, where its activation via dimerization and auto-phosphorylation triggers PLCγ-PKC-Ca2⁺ (vascular permeability), PI3K-Akt (cell survival), and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK (proliferation and migration) pathways [98]. Conversely, VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation. The ability of these ligands to form VEGFR2 heterodimers allows for critical crosstalk between the vascular and lymphatic systems, facilitating tumor dissemination [99]
section_path: Molecular pathogenesis: foundation for targeted therapy
Signaling pathways in colorectal cancer tumorigenesis

claim_01M4YKN7E0HWPB78SXT624CS2F: VEGFR, comprising VEGFR1-3, is the cognate receptor of VEGF, and targeting VEGF/VEGFR is an important therapeutic option in cholangiocarcinoma.

claim_01M4YRR3V7DMNJ5AEEPP3WX96X: Table 1 states that VEGFR1-3 are primarily expressed on endothelial cells and transduce VEGF signals into proliferation, survival and migration of vascular wall cells, controlling angiogenesis and vascular permeability.

claim_01M4YRWQAE78V915V567EJERC2: Table 1 lists regorafenib's targets as VEGFR1-3, TIE2, KIT, RET, RAF1, BRAF, PDGFR, FGFR and colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor, with typical grade 3/4 adverse events of hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, increased lipase and increased blood bilirubin, and indications in metastatic colorectal cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma and gastrointestinal stromal tumour.

claim_01M4YRWQB13APJNNZQ46WS559H: Table 1 lists anlotinib's targets as VEGFR1-3, PDGFR alpha/beta, FGFR1-4 and KIT, with typical grade 3/4 adverse events of hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, lymphocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia and decreased neutrophil count.

claim_01M4YRWQBQE77YNK8AEMHTDKV5: Table 1 lists nintedanib's targets as VEGFR1-3, FGFR1-3, RET, Src, FLT3 and PDGFR-alpha/beta, with typical grade 3/4 adverse events of abnormal liver function tests, abdominal pain and hypertension.

claim_01M4YRWQCB62RJZNKSV7W2YMA2: Table 1 lists sunitinib's targets as VEGFR1-3, PDGFR alpha/beta, c-KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R and RET, with typical grade 3/4 adverse events of asthenia, skin toxicity, hypertension, diarrhoea and haematologic toxicity.

claim_01M4YRWQKKPB4730KCDYG0QTW5: Axitinib is described as an oral, highly potent second-generation TKI targeting VEGFR1-3, approved for advanced renal cell carcinoma, whose VEGFR inhibitory efficacy is approximately 50-450 times greater than that of first-generation TKIs.

claim_01M4YW91P7N2TNBVJ19Y6NXZZP: Sunitinib is an oral TKI targeting multiple receptors including VEGFR1-3, PDGFR-beta, c-KIT, FLT-3 and RET, with demonstrated antitumour activity in advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours.

claim_01M4YWXVC552PXMV18AP71H1M6: The VEGF ligands VEGFA-D and PlGF signal through VEGFR1, VEGFR2 and VEGFR3 plus neuropilin coreceptors; VEGFR2 is central to angiogenesis through PLC-gamma-PKC-Ca2+, PI3K-Akt and Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK pathways, while VEGFC and VEGFD predominantly bind VEGFR3 to induce lymphatic endothelial proliferation, and heterodimer formation allows crosstalk between vascular and lymphatic systems.

claim_01M4YWM8VCZ26QQHRME5SEYX08: Pazopanib is an oral small-molecule inhibitor of multiple tyrosine kinases including VEGFR-1, -2 and -3, PDGFR-alpha and -beta, c-kit, FGFR-1 and -3, and colony-stimulating factor-1 receptor (c-fms).

claim_01M4YXDXW3QEW2XEZ91SSB1FBE: Cediranib potently and selectively inhibits all three VEGF receptors (VEGFR-1, -2 and -3) and is effective in ovarian cancer at 20 mg/day; the stated selectivity means CSF1R and FGFR1 are not covered.
claim_01M4ZH7QHSXTPDJDG0VQW8ZVP5: Only the TKIs were found to inhibit all three VEGF receptors 1–3; of these, axitinib had the strongest inhibitory effect on VEGFR2.
claim_01M4ZK1Y2EQJ8WJS8DBGCYKK2S: Dual blockade of VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 inhibited VEGF-driven angiogenesis, tumor growth, and metastasis by suppressing PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK1/2 signaling pathways.

location.quoted_span: Small-molecule TKIs are administered orally, which likely contributes to variability in TKI exposure [48]. Absorption is the process underlying entry into systemic circulation after oral administration and a significant determinant of oral bioavailability. To be absorbed, a solid dosage form must be dissolved and solubilized before being transported or diffusing across the gut lumen. While disintegration and solubilization mainly occur in the mouth and stomach, the transporter-mediated absorption of most drugs is believed to primarily occur in the small intestine due to its exceptionally high surface area. However, the stomach has been validated to contribute to the transporter-mediated absorption of dasatinib, emphasizing the notion that drug absorption is complex [49]. pH-dependent solubility, gastric emptying time, inhibition of uptake and efflux transporters, and inhibition or induction of enterocyte cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzyme CYP3A4 can also contribute to clinically relevant absorption DDIs [13,16]

location.quoted_span: From a pharmacokinetic perspective, imatinib exhibits rapid oral bioavailability that is not significantly affected by food intake. It has a half‐life of approximately 18 h and is highly protein‐bound (95%), primarily to albumin and α1‐acid glycoprotein. Metabolism is predominantly hepatic, mediated by the CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 enzymes. Notably, imatinib also acts as a competitive inhibitor of these enzymes, creating a significant potential for drug–drug interactions with other PAH therapies metabolized via the same pathway [81]. Elimination is primarily biliary, with a feces‐to‐urine excretion ratio of approximately 5:1

location.quoted_span: Macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) is essential for the entire process from the production of osteoclast precursors to the formation and survival of mature osteoclasts. Upon M-CSF binding to its receptor c-Fms (CSF1R), the receptor is phosphorylated at a specific tyrosine residue in its cytoplasmic tail. These phosphorylated tyrosine residues on the receptor recruit signaling molecules such as growth factor receptor-bound protein 2 (Grb2) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K). This process triggers the activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) and protein kinase B (Akt) pathways, which promote the survival and proliferation of osteoclast precursors

raw.expected_change: Ranks candidates by pooled curated FGFR1 potency; compounds with higher median pChEMBL rise above those with lower or absent curated FGFR1 potency, and candidates with no curated FGFR1 record remain unknown and are not penalised.
raw.falsification_test: If a candidate ranked high on pooled curated FGFR1 pChEMBL fails to inhibit FGFR1 signalling in a functional assay, or a candidate with no curated FGFR1 record is later shown to engage FGFR1 at clinically relevant concentrations, the pooled potency ordering is falsified as the FGFR1 engagement measure for screening.

details.reason: The cited claims report F% values for individual compounds (57%, 39%, 60% in paediatric patients) but none establishes a general ordering or preference for higher human oral bioavailability across the library, and no counter-evidence is cited for the falsification test. nodes.definition: Fraction of an orally administered dose reaching the systemic circulation unchanged, measured in humans and expressed as percent, pooled across independent human clinical or PK studies; animal-only values are not eligible. The value is the median of the family's measurements.

nodes.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
nodes.definition: Fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation unchanged, measured in humans and reported as a percentage. Values are pooled across independent human studies; the median is taken when several measurements exist. Pediatric-only availability values are recorded but flagged as a different population and are not treated as adult absolute F%.

nodes.name: Predicted topological polar surface area (TPSA)
nodes.definition: Model-predicted topological polar surface area in Å² for the compound, read from the ADMET prediction route; lower polarity favours passive diffusion and oral absorption, and values at or below approximately 90 Å² fall in the low-polarity band the cited source associates with improved penetration. Where a compound carries more than one prediction, the pooled value is the median across them.
